architecture.mechanism: Water contamination and iron wear particles physically adsorb onto clutch friction surfaces, degrading the lubricant and destabilizing the friction behavior of wet clutches, which increases the tendency to NVH behavior (noise, vibration, harshness) during engagement.
architecture.intervention: For the AWD system's wet clutch pack (center/coupling clutch), implement lubricant integrity control: seal the housing against water ingress, install magnetic/filtration removal of iron wear particles, and schedule lubricant condition monitoring (water content, particle count, friction coefficient) with fluid replacement before friction behavior degrades.
architecture.expected_effect: Stable clutch friction coefficient under load preserves synchronized, progressive AWD engagement while cornering uphill at highway speed, eliminating the out-of-sync lock-up that produces the metal-on-metal impact noise.
architecture.falsification_test: On a wet-clutch test rig, cycle the AWD clutch pack under uphill cornering load profiles with (a) clean lubricant, (b) water-contaminated lubricant, and (c) water + iron-particle-contaminated lubricant; measure engagement timing synchronization and NVH/impact noise, and verify that contamination produces the out-of-sync impact while clean fluid does not.
